candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — aspiration prevention before anesthesia
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the risk-reduction purpose of preoperative fasting and why fasting intervals differ by intake type and clinical context.

options.A: Fasting eliminates all gastric contents, so aspiration becomes impossible once the interval is completed
options.B: All foods and liquids require the same fasting interval before anesthesia
options.C: Fasting is intended to reduce pulmonary aspiration risk, and recommended intervals differ according to the type of intake and patient/procedure factors
options.D: Fasting is mainly intended to improve surgical exposure rather than reduce aspiration risk

candidate.rationale: ASA preoperative-fasting guidelines are designed to reduce the risk and severity of pulmonary aspiration associated with anesthesia. They distinguish clear liquids and solids rather than applying one universal 'NPO after midnight' interval, and their recommendations are developed for defined patient/procedure contexts rather than guaranteeing an empty stomach or zero aspiration risk. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Preoperative fasting recommendations are intended to mitigate pulmonary aspiration risk and distinguish intake categories rather than impose a single universal interval.
candidate.source_document_title: 2023 ASA Practice Guidelines for Preoperative Fasting: A Modular Update of the 2017 Practice Guidelines
candidate.source_locator: Guideline title/abstract and modular recommendations — fasting guidance to reduce pulmonary aspiration risk; separate clear-liquid/solid/pediatric fasting considerations
candidate.stem: A client scheduled for elective anesthesia asks why the fasting instructions distinguish clear liquids from solid food. Which explanation is most accurate?
